added_failure_basis: The reviewed run records no baseline_suite or after_suite JSON arm, and its only gate log (logs/arms-final-b26da1031.log) carries a head arm of 10 passed with EXIT=0 and a base arm that cannot collect the added test file (EXIT=4, file or directory not found, no failing test id). With no readable pair of arms there is no id a gained commit could have added, so the count of zero records the absence of a measurable delta, not a measured delta of zero.

findings.text: The control's verdict is encoded backwards: the branch that reports CONTROL FAILED exits 0 (line 68) while the branch that reports the refusal exits 1 (line 73). A control whose two forms have not separated therefore returns success and one that did separate returns failure, so any promotion gate reading the status scores a silent failure as the pass.

main records base_status, head_status and control.returncode and then returns, so the driver exits 0 whatever the three arms did; logs/arms-final-b26da1031.log:17 ends EXIT=0 while carrying CONTROL_EXIT=1 and would also end EXIT=0 with a red head arm. The reviewed run's negative_control_log names this log, so the red it records cannot be read from the log's exit status and no admission rule can see the refusal.

extract() and run() re-implement the base-and-head arm runner already owned by scripts/prototypes/diiid_finite_edge_flux/suite_arms.py:36-66, which extracts a revision with git archive, runs pytest under PYTHONPATH and JAX_PLATFORMS, and writes a per-arm log headed with revision, tree and literal command and closed with EXIT=; the addition neither imports nor generalizes that owner, and the missing per-arm log is why the reviewed manifest carries no baseline_suite or after_suite arm.

--directory defaults to the relative name arms, so the run extracts a full repository tree into the working directory it runs in, which is the worktree; the parallel-safety rule puts a temporary extraction under $TMPDIR so it dies with the run's scratch.

mirror_gap recomputes the same vertical residual that _horizontal_reflection already bounded at nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py:2471-2475, so its value is bounded by 32 eps scale for every paired cell and is infinity otherwise; the reported mirror_gap column is now binary rather than a departure, and a cell 1e-12 off symmetry moves from the A group to B although the recheck on this geometry still reads 867 A.

Both cells fed to symmetric_cells are symmetric about their own centre Z, so gaps.shape == (2,) and gaps == 0.0 hold under the owner-based mirror_gap and under the prior centre-based one alike; the assertion cannot fail on the reversion it appears to guard.
The WORST_B empty-section repair is tested only through print_rows, so restoring split.py:191 to a bare print of the WORST_B header leaves the suite green; the repaired call site is never exercised.

The reviewed worktree at b26da1031 carries this file modified and unstaged, so the repairs' narrative and the job ids that re-measured the identity (psi-identity.json over 946 records, split-recheck.json) are not landed; the committed line still quotes psi_current_vs_base_max_abs = 0.0 without citing the receipt that now measures it.
